title: Highway Infrastructure Ltd - 544477 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated total income rose 170.6% YoY to INR 304.3 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR 4.8 crore and PAT was INR 1.1 crore on toll traffic hit.
summary.overview: Management attributed weak Q1 profitability to temporary factors: lower traffic at the Moti Naroli toll project from geopolitical and trade disruption, an NHAI temporary bidding restriction, and voluntary surrender of an unfavourable toll project. Consolidated order book stood at about INR 778 crore at June 30, 2026, with new toll wins in Tamil Nadu (INR 28.7 crore Kozhinjipatti; INR 80 crore Krishnagiri-Thumbipadi NH-44 LoA; INR 120 crore total mentioned in Q&A). Management said traffic has largely normalised outside Western-front regions and expects Q1/Q2 near break-even with recovery in H2. Guidance: FY27 turnover target of INR 850 crore (INR 700 crore toll, rest EPC) and FY28 INR 1,200 crore.

financial_highlights.change: Margin dropped per management; no YoY figure stated

financial_highlights.metric: EPC order book (as cited in Q&A)
financial_highlights.value: approx. INR 507 crore across 24 executable projects

segments.name: Tollway collection
segments.commentary: Asset-light model; Moti Naroli toll hit by lower traffic from geopolitical and trade disruption. New wins: INR 28.7 crore Kozhinjipatti (Tamil Nadu, NH-44) and LoA for INR 80 crore Krishnagiri-Thumbipadi toll; management cited INR 120 crore new Tamil Nadu toll projects in Q&A. Kaza described as outperforming expectations.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Focus on profitable, timely-executable projects in roads, bridges, urban, industrial and commercial. Beverly Hills private project started in Q1: about INR 70 crore, 15-16 months, expected to add at least INR 150 crore EPC revenue (about 40-45% of revenue over 15-16 months per management). Executable EPC orders: about INR 150 crore in FY27 and INR 200 crore in FY28.

segments.name: Real estate
segments.commentary: Named as a vertical in the opening remarks and closing comments; no figures disclosed on the call.

guidance_outlook: FY27 turnover target about INR 850 crore, of which INR 700 crore from toll and rest from EPC.
Management expects Q1 and Q2 to hover around break-even, with rapid recovery in Q3 and Q4 (past pattern); full-year results not expected to be significantly impacted.
Q2 EPC seasonally slow due to monsoon; focus on bidding quality tenders with shorter execution periods.
Management says traffic has largely normalised outside Western-front regions; Western-front recovery will take longer.
capex_capacity: Prequalification (PQ) expected to rise as current EPC projects complete, enabling sole bids for larger tenders.
Geographic expansion: Tamil Nadu entered for the first time; Andhra Pradesh and Telangana priority; West Bengal and Assam under research.
New EPC departments being targeted include MES and CPWD (central), per management.
Renewable energy/EV EPC is a new segment under preparation; no bids or pipeline size disclosed.
demand_pricing: Traffic in regions away from Western-front ports has resumed to normal per management; Western-front recovery slower as factories and trade were hit.
Bid success ratio 25-30% for both toll and EPC.
Management prefers larger toll contracts due to less competition; cited Moti Naroli as roughly 70% larger than Kaza.
Q1 EPC pipeline described as an early accumulation, not the final pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: How has traffic recovered, and will it lift EBITDA margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said traffic in non-Western-front regions is normal; Western front will take time. Margin drop was from the geopolitical situation, expected to recover if no new shocks.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Q1 weakness affect full-year outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Saurabh Mittal said no significant full-year impact: Q1 and Q2 typically near break-even, with stronger Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 and FY28 revenue targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Turnover target INR 850 crore for FY27 and INR 1,200 crore for FY28; FY27 split INR 700 crore toll and rest EPC.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EPC order book and execution timing?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 507 crore EPC order book across 24 executable projects: about INR 150 crore to convert in FY27 and INR 200 crore in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the bid success ratio for toll and EPC?
What is the Beverly Hills project's value and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 70 crore, execution of 15-16 months, expected to contribute about 40-45% of revenue over that period per management.

risks_watch: Western-front traffic and trade recovery pace, and any renewed geopolitical disruption.
Q1 and Q2 near break-even: whether Q2 EBITDA and PAT actually recover as indicated.
FY27 INR 850 crore turnover target requires a steep H2 ramp; INR 700 crore toll target is large relative to current order book.
Concentration in a few states and NHAI bidding restriction status.
Renewable/EV EPC entry and technology initiatives lack quantified targets; management declined to give numbers.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term recovery and growth, but cautious and often non-specific on numbers. Management repeatedly deferred details on renewables, technology initiatives and new states ("unless we have something concrete"), and some answers were vague or repetitive.
key_quotes: Importantly, we have already started witnessing signs of improvement in the traffic trends.

adds.what: Beverly Hills private EPC project (about INR 70 crore, 15-16 months) started in Q1; not productive capacity

growth.why: FY27 turnover target of INR 850 crore (INR 700 crore toll, rest EPC) and FY28 INR 1,200 crore, backed by a ~INR 778 crore consolidated order book and new Tamil Nadu toll wins; no new productive capacity quantified, and Q1/Q2 guided near break-even with recovery in H2.
